title: tidystata
text: English tidystata 把 Stata 风格的数据探索和整理带到 R 中：查看变量、汇总统计、列频数表、生成新变量。变量可以用 tidyselect 方式选择，分组计算用 .。结果都是普通的数据表，可以继续用 R 的常用工具筛选、合并和作图。

title: tidystata
code: # install.packages("pak") pak::pak("socimh/tidystata")

title: tidystata
code: library(tidystata) library(dplyr)

what: findit()：查找 Stata 命令对应的 R 代码
title: tidystata
text: 单独查询命令（如 findit(egen)）返回整个命令族，默认显示最多五种操作。具体查询（如 findit("egen rowmean")）返回一个明确的推荐；含义不明确时保留最多十个相关候选项。print(n = Inf) 展开已返回的结果；查询命令族可浏览更广的操作。同一任务优先推荐 tidystata，其次是 tidyverse，最后是其他包或 base R。可以用逗号添加变量名或提示，例如 findit(tab, sex, region) 或 findit(tab, gen)。在中文环境下运行 R 时，条目说明会显示为中文。全部条目按主题列在从 Stata 到 R中。
code: findit("reg, robust") #> # Heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors [fixest] #> Stata: regress y x1 x2, robust #> R:     fixest::feols(y ~ x1 + x2, data = data, vcov = "hetero") #> # Note: Match fixest covariance small-sample corrections and singleton handling with Stata; the same formula does not guarantee identical standard errors or retained observations. #>  #> # 16 broader regress examples. Browse the family: findit(regress) findit("egen rowmean") #> # Average available values across columns [tidystata] #> Stata: egen z = rowmean(x y) #> R:     mutate(data, z = row_mean(x, y)) #>  #> # 70 broader egen examples. Browse the family: findit(egen)

what: tab()、tab1() 和 tab2()：比较频数表
title: tidystata
text: 用 lifeexp 中的地区和一个新类别作比较：预期寿命是否达到 70 岁。region:lexp_70 选择这两列。 tab() 统计每种实际出现的组合的频数，并给出百分比。 tab1() 返回一个命名列表，为每个变量分别生成频数表。 tab2() 将联合频数排列成交叉表，地区为行，预期寿命类别为列。 也可以对连续变量制表。当不同取值较多时，用 print_interval() 查看等间隔选取的行，或用 print_headtail() 查看开头和结尾。这些函数只缩短显示内容，仍保留完整的频数表。

what: 在 R 中直接查询
title: 从 Stata 到 R
text: findit() 在 R 中查询同一份列表。单个 Stata 命令可以不加引号，更长的内容需要加引号；支持 Stata 的标准缩写。说明文字随 R 的语言设置显示为中文或英文，两种语言的查询都可使用。 也可以查询 R 函数（findit(left_join)），或直接提问（findit("如何删除重复行")）。 单独查询命令（例如 findit(egen)）时，返回整个命令族，默认显示最多五种操作。 具体查询（例如 findit("egen rowmean")）在答案明确时返回一个结果；有歧义的查询 最多保留十个相关候选。不带参数的 findit() 返回完整列表。 逗号分隔的变量名会填入兼容的示例，例如 findit(tab, sex, region)。匹配的提示词 （例如 findit(tab, gen)）可将结果缩小到一个答案。print(n = Inf) 展开返回的候选、 差异说明和参考链接。末尾提示分别列出尚未显示的相关结果和命令族中更广泛的操作； 使用 findit(egen) 浏览整个命令族。同一操作内依次优先推荐 tidystata、tidyverse、 其他包或基础 R。findit(dplyr::filter) 这样的包限定查询可以区分同名函数。 本指南包含 514 个命令族、181 个 Stata 函数和 3 个运算符，共有 1721 个不同的 Stata 示例和 1877 条 R 对照示例。缩写及同一任务的其他 R 实现不会增加命令数量。 R 函数索引包含 969 个函数与包的组合。
code: findit(reg) #> # Linear regression [stats] #> Stata: regress y x1 x2 #> R:     fit <- lm(y ~ x1 + x2, data = data) #> # Note: summary(fit) shows the coefficient table; broom::tidy(fit) returns it as a data frame. #>  #> # Fit linear regression through the origin [stats] #> Stata: regress y x z, noconstant #> R:     stats::lm(y ~ x + z - 1, data=data) #> # Note: OLS coefficient correspondence requires the same complete-case sample, contrasts and weights. R returns an lm object; Stata coefficient tables and stored estimates have a different structure. #>  #> # Include two continuous main effects and their interaction [stats] #> Stata: regress y c.x##c.z #> R:     stats::lm(y ~ x * z, data=data) #> # Note: OLS coefficient correspondence requires the same complete-case sample, contrasts and weights. R returns an lm object; Stata coefficient tables and stored estimates have a different structure. #>  #> # Fit a quadratic regression [stats] #> Stata: regress y c.x##c.x #> R:     stats::lm(y ~ x + I(x^2), data=data) #> # Note: OLS coefficient correspondence requires the same complete-case sample, contrasts and weights. R returns an lm object; Stata coefficient tables and stored estimates have a different structure. #>  #> # Adjust regression for a categorical predictor [stats] #> Stata: regress y i.g c.x #> R:     stats::lm(y ~ factor(g) + x, data=data) #> # Note: OLS coefficient correspondence requires the same complete-case sample, contrasts and weights. R returns an lm object; Stata coefficient tables and stored estimates have a different structure. #>  #> # 13 more relevant examples. To see them all: findit(reg) |> print(n = Inf) findit("merge 1:1 id, keep(match)") #> # Keep matched rows only [dplyr] #> Stata: merge 1:1 id using data2, keep(match) #> R:     inner_join(data1, data2, by = "id") #> # Note: dplyr retains overlapping non-key columns with suffixes instead of Stata master values, creates no _merge, and does not enforce a declared 1:1 key constraint. #>  #> # merge() [base]: Merge two data frames (base R) #>   Related Stata: merge #>  #> # 12 broader merge examples. Browse the family: findit(merge)

title: 从 Stata 到 R
text: destring()（as_numeric()）将数值文本转换为数字，tostring() （as_character()）将底层编码转换为文本。分类变量使用 encode() 将字符串 转换为带值标签的整数编码，使用 decode() 将值标签读为文本。字符输入按排序顺序 从 1 开始分配新编码；因子输入保留现有整数编号及全部水平。 encode(decode(x)) 不一定恢复原编码。字符列应在分组之前编码，以便所有行使用 同一套编码与标签。 下表涵盖 tidystata 和其他常用 R 包，包括建模、长宽转换、调查分析和作图。 面板滞后、超前和差分可使用 tidystata 的 stata_lag()、stata_lead() 和 stata_diff()；指定时间列，并用 .区分面板。 索引按字母顺序排列，对照表按主题分组，并依次按命令、推荐顺序和示例排序。 运行某个示例需要其标注的 R 包；findit() 本身不会加载或安装这些参考包。 包标签只列出主要实现包，并不列出所有辅助依赖；R 函数索引标明其他函数及其所属包。 以 与 Stata 有差异 开头的说明表示 R 代码完成相同任务，但默认设置、缺失值处理、 估计方法或输出形式有所不同，说明会列出具体差异。其余说明是使用提示。多数 R 示例在构建目录时 运行核验，检查的是 R 代码本身，并非与 Stata 的数值一致性检验。缺失值比较、权重、因子参照组、连接规则和标准误修正尤其需要核对。 已知缺口会明确说明，相关搜索结果不代表已经实现查询中尚未支持的语法。 下表中，data 是你的数据，data1 和 data2 是合并时的主数据和被合并数据，fit R returns an lm object; Stata coefficient tables and stored estimates have a different structure. #>  #> # Include two continuous main effects and their interaction [stats] #> Stata: regress y c.x##c.z #> R:     stats::lm(y ~ x * z, data=data) #> # Note: OLS coefficient correspondence requires the same complete-case sample, contrasts and weights. R returns an lm object; Stata coefficient tables and stored estimates have a different structure. #>  #> # Fit a quadratic regression [stats] #> Stata: regress y c.x##c.x #> R:     stats::lm(y ~ x + I(x^2), data=data) #> # Note: OLS coefficient correspondence requires the same complete-case sample, contrasts and weights. title: Containers, grouping and missing values
text: New tables tab, summ, codebook variables families preserve base data frame, tibble data.table input. list result remains list, table inside follows rule. explicit output option takes precedence. corr(), pwcorr(), spearman(), misstable() duplicates_report() exceptions: always return tibbles. supported, .type selects output form: every function accepts every value. tab2() fre2() still return lists multiple pairs explicit .groups, even .type = "tibble" .type = "flextable". corr(), pwcorr() spearman() use .wide choose layout; layouts return tibbles. data-frame subclasses reconstructed newly shaped tables. Vectors, result ds() row_mean(), keep intentional vector output. New data.table summaries retain input keys indexes. as_dummy(.remove = TRUE) reports error result data.table rows columns; retain source identifier column case. data.table inputs follow rule: formatted table, install flextable request .type = "flextable":
code: library(tidystata) library(dplyr) #>  #> Attaching package: 'dplyr' #> The following object is masked from 'package:tidystata': #>  #>     recode #> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats': #>  #>     filter, lag #> The following objects are masked from 'package:base': #>  #>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union  df <- data.frame(   group = c("A", "A", "B", NA),   answer = c("yes", NA, "no", "yes"),   score = c(2, NA, 6, 8) ) tbl <- tibble::as_tibble(df)  class(tab(df, answer)) #> [1] "data.frame" class(tab(tbl, answer)) #> [1] "tbl_df"     "tbl"        "data.frame" class(summ(df, score)) #> [1] "data.frame" class(summ(tbl, score)) #> [1] "tbl_df"     "tbl"        "data.frame" base_tables <- tab1(df, answer, group) class(base_tables) #> [1] "list" class(base_tables$answer) #> [1] "data.frame" class(fre(df, answer, .type = "tibble")) #> [1] "tbl_df"     "tbl"        "data.frame" class(ds(df, .type = "tibble")) #> [1] "tbl_df"     "tbl"        "data.frame" class(summ(df, score, .type = "tibble")) #> [1] "tbl_df"     "tbl"        "data.frame" class(tabstat(df, score, .type = "tibble")) #> [1] "tbl_df"     "tbl"        "data.frame" if (requireNamespace("data.table", quietly = TRUE)) {   dt <- data.table::as.data.table(df)   class(tab(dt, answer))   class(summ(dt, score)) } #> [1] "data.table" "data.frame" if (requireNamespace("flextable", quietly = TRUE)) {   rich <- fre(tbl, answer, .type = "flextable")   class(rich) } #> [1] "flextable"

title: Containers, grouping and missing values
text: Summary inventory results ungrouped. Grouping keys remain ordinary columns reported. tab(), tab1(), fre(), fre1(), summ() tabstat(), .= NULL inherits existing groups; explicit .replaces . tab2() fre2() require explicit .grouped cross-tabulations; otherwise, tabulate whole input regardless existing groups. Cross-tabulation tab2() fre2() returns one table per group, list named group: One-way tabulations use observations within group percent cum, zero--100 scale. valid valid_cum exclude missing measured values. Missing grouping keys ordinary groups. summaries, valid_pct instead fraction zero one. summ(.missing = FALSE) removes missing grouping keys; numeric calculations always omit missing measured values.
code: grouped <- group_by(tbl, group) tab(grouped, answer) #> # A tibble: 4 × 7 #>   group answer     n percent   cum valid valid_cum #>   <chr> <chr>  <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1 A     yes        1      50    50   100       100 #> 2 A     NA         1      50   100    NA        NA #> 3 B     no         1     100   100   100       100 #> 4 NA    yes        1     100   100   100       100 summary <- summ(grouped, score, .stat = c("n", "mean", "missing")) summary #> # A tibble: 3 × 5 #>   group type      n  mean missing #>   <chr> <chr> <int> <dbl>   <int> #> 1 A     dbl       1     2       1 #> 2 B     dbl       1     6       0 #> 3 NA    dbl       1     8       0 group_vars(summary) #> character(0) summ(grouped, score, .by = answer, .stat = c("n", "mean")) #> # A tibble: 3 × 4 #>   answer type      n  mean #>   <chr>  <chr> <int> <dbl> #> 1 no     dbl       1     6 #> 2 yes    dbl       2     5 #> 3 NA     dbl       0    NA crossed <- tab2(df, answer, score, .by = group) names(crossed) #> [1] "group = A"  "group = B"  "group = NA" tab(tbl, answer) #> # A tibble: 3 × 6 #>   answer     n percent   cum valid valid_cum #>   <chr>  <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1 no         1      25    25  33.3      33.3 #> 2 yes        2      50    75  66.7     100   #> 3 NA         1      25   100  NA        NA summ(tbl, score, .stat = c("n", "miss_n", "valid_pct", "mean")) #> # A tibble: 1 × 5 #>   type      n miss_n valid_pct  mean #>   <chr> <int>  <int>     <dbl> <dbl> #> 1 dbl       3      1      0.75  5.33 summ(tbl, score, .by = group, .missing = FALSE, .stat = c("n", "mean")) #> # A tibble: 2 × 4 #>   group type      n  mean #>   <chr> <chr> <int> <dbl> #> 1 A     dbl       1     2 #> 2 B     dbl       1     6

title: Containers, grouping and missing values
text: ungrouped numeric column observations remains summary n = 0 NA statistics, including sum. -missing row instead row sum zero row mean NA. Empty selections give empty results tabulation; row helpers require least one column. Matrix columns supported tabulation column-summary interfaces.
code: empty <- tbl[0, ] summ(empty, score, .stat = c("n", "sum", "mean")) #> # A tibble: 1 × 4 #>   type      n   sum  mean #>   <chr> <int> <dbl> <dbl> #> 1 dbl       0    NA    NA tab1(tbl, starts_with("absent")) #> named list()  missing <- tibble(a = c(NA_real_, NA_real_), b = c(NA_real_, 4)) summ(missing, a, .stat = c("n", "sum", "mean")) #> Warning: a is entirely missing; retained with n = 0. #> # A tibble: 1 × 4 #>   type      n   sum  mean #>   <chr> <int> <dbl> <dbl> #> 1 dbl       0    NA    NA row_sum(missing) #> [1] 0 4 row_mean(missing) #> [1] NA  4

title: Containers, grouping and missing values
text: Variable labels describe columns; value labels describe particular values. Numeric calculations exclude SPSS user-missing codes Stata tagged missing values. Tabulations report missing categories alongside observed values. Summary statistics labelled numeric measurements use underlying values exclude SPSS user-missing codes. Factors use level codes warn; choose measurements deliberately instead averaging category codes. decode() displays value labels present, recode every labelled refusal ordinary NA. misstable() also accepts matrix nested data-frame columns, using vctrs missingness complete rows. Ordinary list columns count scalar NA elements missing NULL observed. Structured list-backed matrices instead follow vctrs cell rules: NULL cells missing scalar NA cells observed. See misstable() output forms.
code: labelled <- tibble(   response = haven::labelled_spss(     c(1, 2, 99, NA),     labels = c(Yes = 1, No = 2, Refused = 99),     na_values = 99,     label = "Interview response"   ) ) variables(labelled) #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>   name     label              #>   <chr>    <chr>              #> 1 response Interview response codebook(labelled) #> # A tibble: 1 × 5 #>   variable label              type             n unique #>   <chr>    <chr>              <chr>        <int>  <int> #> 1 response Interview response double+label     2      2 tab(labelled, response) #> # A tibble: 4 × 6 #>   response              n percent   cum valid valid_cum #>   <dbl+lbl>         <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1  1 [Yes]              1      25    25    50        50 #> 2  2 [No]               1      25    50    50       100 #> 3 99 (NA) [Refused]     1      25    75    NA        NA #> 4 NA                    1      25   100    NA        NA decode(labelled$response) #> [1] "Yes"     "No"      "Refused" NA

title: Containers, grouping and missing values
text: Default list mode keeps numeric statistics numeric table. Calendar locations min, mean max formatted dates date-times, spread sd stays difftime. Table mode combines families. location column shared numeric calendar rows becomes character, spread column becomes plain number days dates seconds date-times, unit shown type column. SD uses sample denominator. Percentiles use Stata’s rule; example, quartiles 1:4 1.5 3.5. See summ() formulas, weights statistics.
code: mixed <- tibble(score = c(2, 4), day = as.Date("2024-01-01") + c(0, 2)) separate <- summ(mixed, .stat = c("n", "min", "mean", "sd", "max")) #> A list is returned as statistics are heterogeneous. names(separate) #> [1] "numeric" "date" separate$numeric #> # A tibble: 1 × 7 #>   name  type      n   min  mean    sd   max #>   <chr> <chr> <int> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> #> 1 score dbl       2     2     3  1.41     4 separate$date #> # A tibble: 1 × 7 #>   name  type      n min        mean       sd            max        #>   <chr> <chr> <int> <chr>      <chr>      <drtn>        <chr>      #> 1 day   date      2 2024-01-01 2024-01-02 1.414214 days 2024-01-03 class(separate$date$sd) #> [1] "difftime" combined <- summ(mixed, .type = "table", .stat = c("n", "min", "mean", "sd", "max")) combined #> # A tibble: 2 × 7 #>   name  type            n min        mean          sd max        #>   <chr> <chr>       <int> <chr>      <chr>      <dbl> <chr>      #> 1 score dbl             2 2          3           1.41 4          #> 2 day   date [days]     2 2024-01-01 2024-01-02  1.41 2024-01-03 class(combined$sd) #> [1] "numeric"

title: Containers, grouping and missing values
text: preview still contains 12 rows. n total display budget, split beginning end. single row dots marks omitted middle. Interval previews show approximately evenly spaced positions without separator rows; sort first position represent meaningful order. styles report many rows omitted display. print_headtail() print_interval() print invisibly return complete input. useful tabulating continuous variable many distinct values. tab() counts distinct value separately sorts values ascending order default: print_interval() shows evenly spaced rows across sorted table; print_headtail() shows beginning end. Neither helper bins values, removes rows returned table, changes counts percentages. unpreview() removes persistent display setting. Supported dplyr/tidyr operations carry preview settings forward following container grouping rules. Wrapping unwrapping data.table copies ; later native data.table mutations retain ordinary reference semantics.
code: long <- tibble(id = 1:12, value = (1:12)^2) view <- preview_headtail(long, n = 4) view #> # A tibble: 12 × 2 #>       id value #>    <int> <dbl> #>  1     1     1 #>  2     2     4 #>  ⋮     ⋮     ⋮ #> 11    11   121 #> 12    12   144 #> # ... 8 rows omitted in the middle; use print(x, n = Inf) to show all rows. nrow(view) #> [1] 12 sum(view$value) #> [1] 650 preview_interval(long, n = 4) #> # A tibble: 12 × 2 #>       id value #>    <int> <dbl> #>  1     1     1 #>  5     5    25 #>  8     8    64 #> 12    12   144 #> # ... 8 rows omitted between displayed positions; use print(x, n = Inf) to show #> # all rows. ordinary <- unpreview(view) identical(ordinary, long) #> [1] TRUE lifeexp_counts <- tab(lifeexp, lexp) print_interval(lifeexp_counts, n = 6) #> # A tibble: 20 × 6 #>     lexp     n percent    cum valid valid_cum #>    <dbl> <int>   <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> #>  1    57     1    1.47   1.47  1.47      1.47 #>  5    64     3    4.41  11.8   4.41     11.8  #>  9    68     3    4.41  25     4.41     25    #> 12    71     6    8.82  47.1   8.82     47.1  #> 16    75     4    5.88  72.1   5.88     72.1  #> 20    79     6    8.82 100     8.82    100    #> # ... 14 rows omitted between displayed positions; use print(x, n = Inf) to #> # show all rows. print_headtail(lifeexp_counts, n = 6) #> # A tibble: 20 × 6 #>     lexp     n percent    cum valid valid_cum #>    <dbl> <int>   <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> #>  1    57     1    1.47   1.47  1.47      1.47 #>  2    61     1    1.47   2.94  1.47      2.94 #>  3    62     2    2.94   5.88  2.94      5.88 #>  ⋮     ⋮     ⋮     ⋮      ⋮     ⋮         ⋮   #> 18    77     5    7.35  85.3   7.35     85.3  #> 19    78     4    5.88  91.2   5.88     91.2  #> 20    79     6    8.82 100     8.82    100    #> # ... 14 rows omitted in the middle; use print(x, n = Inf) to show all rows.

title: Getting started with tidystata
text: codebook() gives one row per variable. variables() reports names variable labels, ds() returns character vector names. variables_search() searches names labels, can find variable description:
code: library(tidystata) library(dplyr) #>  #> Attaching package: 'dplyr' #> The following object is masked from 'package:tidystata': #>  #>     recode #> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats': #>  #>     filter, lag #> The following objects are masked from 'package:base': #>  #>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union  survey <- tibble(   id = 1:6,   group = c("A", "A", "A", "B", "B", NA),   response = c("yes", "no", NA, "yes", "yes", "no"),   score1 = c(2, 4, NA, 6, 8, 10),   score2 = c(4, NA, NA, 8, 10, 12) ) attr(survey$score1, "label") <- "First assessment score"  codebook(survey) #> # A tibble: 5 × 5 #>   variable label                  type          n unique #>   <chr>    <chr>                  <chr>     <int>  <int> #> 1 id       NA                     integer       6      6 #> 2 group    NA                     character     5      2 #> 3 response NA                     character     5      2 #> 4 score1   First assessment score double        5      5 #> 5 score2   NA                     double        4      4 variables(survey) #> # A tibble: 5 × 2 #>   name     label                  #>   <chr>    <chr>                  #> 1 id       NA                     #> 2 group    NA                     #> 3 response NA                     #> 4 score1   First assessment score #> 5 score2   NA ds(survey, starts_with("score")) #> [1] "score1" "score2" variables_search(survey, "assessment") #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>   name   label                  #>   <chr>  <chr>                  #> 1 score1 First assessment score select_or_transmute(survey, id, starts_with("score")) #> # A tibble: 6 × 3 #>      id score1 score2 #>   <int>  <dbl>  <dbl> #> 1     1      2      4 #> 2     2      4     NA #> 3     3     NA     NA #> 4     4      6      8 #> 5     5      8     10 #> 6     6     10     12

title: Getting started with tidystata
text: counts sum six, including missing response. tab() returns observed categories counts percentages. fre() adds total rows; tab2() puts categories second variable columns. Use tab1() want separate one-way tables instead joint table: returned objects contain data. example, select categories occurring ordinary pipeline:
code: counts <- tab(survey, response) counts #> # A tibble: 3 × 6 #>   response     n percent   cum valid valid_cum #>   <chr>    <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1 no           2    33.3  33.3    40        40 #> 2 yes          3    50    83.3    60       100 #> 3 NA           1    16.7 100      NA        NA sum(counts$n) #> [1] 6  fre(survey, response) #> # A tibble: 5 × 6 #>   response        n percent   cum valid valid_cum #>   <chr>       <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1 no              2    33.3  33.3    40        40 #> 2 yes             3    50    83.3    60       100 #> 3 Valid Total     5    83.3  NA     100        NA #> 4 NA              1    16.7 100      NA        NA #> 5 Total           6   100    NA      NA        NA tab2(survey, group, response) #> # A tibble: 3 × 4 #>   `group \\ response`    no   yes  `NA` #>   <chr>               <int> <int> <int> #> 1 A                       1     1     1 #> 2 B                       0     2     0 #> 3 NA                      1     0     0 tables <- tab1(survey, group, response) tables$response #> # A tibble: 3 × 6 #>   value     n percent   cum valid valid_cum #>   <chr> <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1 no        2    33.3  33.3    40        40 #> 2 yes       3    50    83.3    60       100 #> 3 NA        1    16.7 100      NA        NA tab(survey, response) |>   filter(n > 1) #> # A tibble: 2 × 6 #>   response     n percent   cum valid valid_cum #>   <chr>    <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1 no           2    33.3  33.3    40        40 #> 2 yes          3    50    83.3    60       100

title: Getting started with tidystata
text: Select numeric measurements deliberately. Codes attached categories automatically meaningful measurements. summ() can return several statistics. tabstat() selects means default. omit missing measured values numeric calculations. Missing grouping keys remain group unless request .missing = FALSE: Numeric-summaries return table. numeric calendar measurements combined, default can list tables. companion vignette("containers--missing-values", package = "tidystata") explains types missing-value conventions.
code: summ(survey, score1, score2, .stat = c("n", "mean", "sd", "missing")) #> # A tibble: 2 × 6 #>   name   type      n  mean    sd missing #>   <chr>  <chr> <int> <dbl> <dbl>   <int> #> 1 score1 dbl       5   6    3.16       1 #> 2 score2 dbl       4   8.5  3.42       2 tabstat(survey, score1, score2, .by = group) #> # A tibble: 6 × 4 #>   group name   type   mean #>   <chr> <chr>  <chr> <dbl> #> 1 A     score1 dbl       3 #> 2 A     score2 dbl       4 #> 3 B     score1 dbl       7 #> 4 B     score2 dbl       9 #> 5 NA    score1 dbl      10 #> 6 NA    score2 dbl      12 mean(survey$score1, na.rm = TRUE) #> [1] 6 summ(survey, score1, .by = group, .missing = FALSE, .stat = c("n", "mean")) #> # A tibble: 2 × 4 #>   group type      n  mean #>   <chr> <chr> <int> <dbl> #> 1 A     dbl       2     3 #> 2 B     dbl       2     7

title: Getting started with tidystata
text: Row helpers return vectors, making convenient mutate(). pick() makes columns combined explicit. third row observed score, average NA observed count zero. Row sums use zero -missing row, column summaries use NA sum observations. Character measurements can parsed explicitly, sentinel values can replaced calculations: destring() reads numbers currency symbols, thousands separators percent signs; text, "10 kg", becomes NA warning unless remove ignore = "kg". xtile() uses Stata’s percentile cutpoints keeps tied values together; ties can leave groups empty. stata_recode() follows Stata’s recode: 1:5 range 1 5, including decimals, values rule matches kept.
code: prepared <- survey |>   mutate(     average = row_mean(pick(score1, score2)),     observed = row_non_miss(pick(score1, score2))   ) prepared #> # A tibble: 6 × 7 #>      id group response score1 score2 average observed #>   <int> <chr> <chr>     <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>    <int> #> 1     1 A     yes           2      4       3        2 #> 2     2 A     no            4     NA       4        1 #> 3     3 A     NA           NA     NA      NA        0 #> 4     4 B     yes           6      8       7        2 #> 5     5 B     yes           8     10       9        2 #> 6     6 NA    no           10     12      11        2 destring(c("1,200", "2,500", NA)) #> [1] 1200 2500   NA mvdecode(c(1, -99, 3), -99) #> [1]  1 NA  3 xtile(1:8, 4) #> [1] [1,2.5]   [1,2.5]   (2.5,4.5] (2.5,4.5] (4.5,6.5] (4.5,6.5] (6.5,8]   #> [8] (6.5,8]   #> Levels: [1,2.5] < (2.5,4.5] < (4.5,6.5] < (6.5,8] stata_recode(c(2, 4.5, 7, 12), 1:5 ~ 1, 6:10 ~ 2) #> [1]  1  1  2 12

code: # Keep a successful result capture(mean(1:10)) #> [1] 5.5  # Suppress warnings and messages capture({   message("Calculating")   mean(1:10) }, quiet = TRUE) #> [1] 5.5  # A new object receives NULL on error, with a failure message result <- capture(stop("Cannot calculate")) #> Captured expression did not complete. #> ℹ Changes made before the error may persist. #> Caused by error: #> ! Cannot calculate  result #> NULL  # A failed assignment leaves the original data unchanged data <- tibble::tibble(x = 1:3) capture(data <- dplyr::mutate(data, y = missing_var * 2)) #> Captured expression did not complete. #> ℹ Changes made before the error may persist. #> Caused by error in `dplyr::mutate()`: #> ℹ In argument: `y = missing_var * 2`. #> Caused by error: #> ! object 'missing_var' not found data  # Still contains only x #> # A tibble: 3 × 1 #>       x #>   <int> #> 1     1 #> 2     2 #> 3     3  # Successful assignments are preserved before an error capture({   data <- dplyr::mutate(data, y = x * 2)   data <- dplyr::mutate(data, z = missing_var * 2) }) #> Captured expression did not complete. #> ℹ Changes made before the error may persist. #> Caused by error in `dplyr::mutate()`: #> ℹ In argument: `z = missing_var * 2`. #> Caused by error: #> ! object 'missing_var' not found data  # Contains x and y #> # A tibble: 3 × 2 #>       x     y #>   <int> <dbl> #> 1     1     2 #> 2     2     4 #> 3     3     6  # A pipeline updates the data only if all steps succeed capture(   data <- data |>     dplyr::mutate(z = x + 1) |>     dplyr::mutate(w = missing_var * 2) ) #> Captured expression did not complete. #> ℹ Changes made before the error may persist. #> Caused by error in `dplyr::mutate()`: #> ℹ In argument: `w = missing_var * 2`. #> Caused by error: #> ! object 'missing_var' not found data  # Still contains x and y #> # A tibble: 3 × 2 #>       x     y #>   <int> <dbl> #> 1     1     2 #> 2     2     4 #> 3     3     6

`assert` allows only matched.  # Keep matched rows only stata_merge(people, income, "1:1", by = "id", keep = "match", report = FALSE) #> # A tibble: 2 × 4 #>      id   age income .merge  #>   <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <fct>   #> 1     2    41     10 matched #> 2     3    25     20 matched  # Many people per household members <- tibble::tibble(hh = c(1, 1, 2), person = 1:3) households <- tibble::tibble(hh = 1:2, region = c("north", "south")) stata_merge(members, households, "m:1", by = "hh") #> Result                            Rows #> -------------------------------------- #> Not matched                          0 #>     from master                      0  (.merge == "master only") #>     from using                       0  (.merge == "using only") #>  #> Matched                              3  (.merge == "matched") #> -------------------------------------- #> # A tibble: 3 × 4 #>      hh person region .merge  #>   <dbl>  <int> <chr>  <fct>   #> 1     1      1 north  matched #> 2     1      2 north  matched #> 3     2      3 south  matched

title: Recode numeric values with Stata-style rules — stata_recode
text: Output type Integer input stays integer every code .default whole number within integer range, 1:5 ~ 1 promote double. Double input stays double. Fractions, --range numbers, infinities, NaN, tagged missing codes defaults require double output; ordinary NA promote integer input. input modified. Matching left side rule read evaluation: :b selects closed range <= x <= b, including decimals, like Stata's /b. Thus 1:5 matches 4.5, rather enumerating integers. Non-missing values match exactly; missing value set matches every missing type, . Rules match input replacements, SPSS missing-value conversion. first matching rule wins, 1 ~ 2, 2 ~ 1 swaps codes. Supply .default replace unmatched elements, including missing ones. left side, bare min max mean -Inf Inf. Unlike Stata's keywords, refer observed extrema: min:min select smallest observed code. Calls min(x) still evaluate normally. Bounds, like value sets, must ordinary integer double numbers; convert classed numbers integer64 explicitly. Common rule translations : Like Stata's recode, functions operate numeric values. text, use dplyr::recode_values() dplyr::replace_values() dplyr 1.2.0 later, dplyr::case_match() older versions. factors, use forcats::fct_recode() forcats::fct_collapse(). alias recode() shares name dplyr::recode(). title: Recode numeric values with Stata-style rules — stata_recode
code: # Keep unmatched values x <- c(1, 4.5, 6, 9, 12, NA) stata_recode(x, 1:5 ~ 1, 6:10 ~ 2) #> [1]  1  1  2  2 12 NA  # Replace unmatched values with missing stata_recode(x, 1:5 ~ 1, 6:10 ~ 2, .default = NA) #> [1]  1  1  2  2 NA NA  # Unbounded intervals and missing values stata_recode(x, min:5 ~ 0, 6:max ~ 1, NA ~ 9) #> [1] 0 0 1 1 1 9  # Swap codes without cascading replacements stata_recode(c(1, 2, 3), 1 ~ 2, 2 ~ 1) #> [1] 2 1 3  # Assign new value labels stata_recode(x, Low = 1:5 ~ 1, High = 6:max ~ 2) #> <labelled<double>[6]> #> [1]  1  1  2  2  2 NA #>  #> Labels: #>  value label #>      1   Low #>      2  High  # Create a new variable d <- data.frame(score = c(2, 7, 11)) dplyr::mutate(   d,   group = stata_recode(score, 1:5 ~ 1, 6:10 ~ 2, .default = NA) ) #>   score group #> 1     2     1 #> 2     7     2 #> 3    11    NA  # Apply rules to several variables and prefix the new names items <- data.frame(item1 = c(1, 7, 9), item2 = c(3, 8, 12)) dplyr::mutate(   items,   dplyr::across(     dplyr::everything(),     function(v) stata_recode(v, 1:5 ~ 1, 6:10 ~ 2, 11:15 ~ 3),     .names = "r_{.col}"   ) ) #>   item1 item2 r_item1 r_item2 #> 1     1     3       1       1 #> 2     7     8       2       2 #> 3     9    12       2       3

text: default, std(x) computes (x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(x, na.rm = TRUE) using sample standard deviation. pc(x) computes 100 * x / sum(x, na.rm = TRUE), percentile ranks. title: Summary statistics — summ
text: Statistics calculated separately selected variable group. formulas use non-missing measured values x1, ..., xn, n denoting count xbar arithmetic mean. Unless weights supplied, calculations unweighted. Counts completeness type: Variable type (metadata, calculated statistic). n: Number non-missing values. unique: Number distinct non-missing values. miss_n: Number missing values (alias: missing). valid_pct: Proportion rows non-missing value, 0 1; n / (n + miss_n) without weights. multiplied 100. Location totals min, max: Smallest largest observed values. sum: Arithmetic total, sum(x). Available numeric variables . mean: Arithmetic mean, sum(x) / n. q1 (p25), median (p50), q3 (p75): 25th, 50th, 75th percentiles, respectively. p0 p100: requested percentile, including decimal percentages p2.5. Percentiles follow Stata's rule, R's default stats::quantile() type 7. sorted observations percentile p, set h = n * p / 100. h integer, use observation position ceiling(h); h integer 1 n - 1, average observations positions h h + 1. endpoints minimum (p0) maximum (p100). example, 25th percentile 1:4 1.5, rather 1.75 type 7. Variation precision sd: Sample standard deviation, sqrt(sum((x - xbar)^2) / (n - 1)). se: Standard error mean, sd / sqrt(n). mad: Median absolute deviation median, multiplied 1.4826, stats::mad(). statistic reported Stata's summarize command. iqr: Interquartile range, q3 - q1, using percentiles . Distribution shape Define mk = sum((x - xbar)^k) / n, kth population central moment. skew: Skewness, m3 / m2^(3/2). kurtosis: Pearson kurtosis, m4 / m2^2. normal distribution kurtosis 3, 0 (excess kurtosis). Undefined statistics NA (example, sd n < 2 shape statistics constant variables). Frequency weights (.wt_type = "frequency") use weights given. reported n W; non-integer weights permitted. Analytic weights (.wt_type = "analytic") rescaled within variable group W equals number observed values. Thus n remains sample-count scale. Mean spread: mean = sum(w * x) / W, sd = sqrt(sum(w * (x - mean)^2) / (W - 1)), se = sd / sqrt(W). two weight types give mean can give different sd se values. NA W <= 1. Shape: Skewness kurtosis use weighted population central moments, mk = sum(w * (x - mean)^k) / W. remain defined W > 0 population spread nonzero, including fractional W <= 1. Quantiles MAD: Percentiles use Stata's weighted percentile rule, replacing positions cumulative weights; weighted mad uses corresponding weighted medians. min max exclude zero-weight rows. Totals counts: sum sum(w * x) using original, unrescaled weights, even analytic weights. unique, miss_n, valid_pct continue use unweighted row counts. reported se descriptive account complex survey design. survey inference, use functions survey::svymean(). title: Frequency tables and cross-tabulations — tab
text: Create Stata-style frequency tables using joint counts, separate one-way tables, pairwise cross-tabulations: tab(): Count combinations selected variables one long-format table frequencies percentages. fre(): Count combinations tab(), adding totals displaying value labels. tab1(): Tabulate variable separately, returning one-way frequency table variable. fre1(): Tabulate variable separately tab1(), adding totals displaying value labels. tab2(): Cross-tabulate every pair selected variables, returning wide contingency tables categories rows columns. fre2(): Cross-tabulate every pair tab2(), adding marginal totals displaying row-category labels. Column headers retain category codes.

title: Frequency tables and cross-tabulations — tab
text: Counts percentages following five columns produced tab(), tab1(), fre(), fre1(). group, let n_i count category (category combination) , N count across categories, N_valid count excluding observations missing measured variable. percentages 0–100 scale. n: Number observations category, sum weights weighted. percent: Percentage observations, 100 * n_i / N, including missing measured values denominator. cum: Cumulative percent, summed displayed category order. valid: Percentage complete observations, 100 * n_i / N_valid. NA categories missing measured values. valid_cum: Cumulative valid, displayed order, omitting missing measured categories. Thus percent corresponds Stata's tabulate, missing, valid uses denominator tabulate without missing. missing grouping key make measured value invalid. Missing values category order Missing measured values kept categories shown last. Missingness includes NA, NaN, tagged missing values, SPSS user-missing codes ranges; empty strings observed values. Factors follow level order; categories sorted value unless .desc requests frequency order. List-column elements counted complete values, flattened. Weighted counts percentages Let w_j weight observation j group. Frequency weights (.wt_type = "frequency"): Category counts n_i = sum(w_j) observations category. Weights need integers. Analytic weights (.wt_type = "analytic"): Weights rescaled within group sum number rows. Category counts sum rescaled weights, overall count stays sample-size scale. Percentages: weight types give percentages normalization factor cancels group. Cumulative valid percentages use corresponding weighted counts denominators. Rows missing weights excluded; negative weights allowed. ... omitted, weight column tabulated. Totals value labels fre() fre1() append "Total" row within group may add "Valid Total" "Missing Total" subtotals. fre2() adds marginal total row column. fre() fre1() display value labels; fre2() displays row-category labels keeps column headers based category codes. tab() tab1() retain underlying category codes types. Totals may convert category column character introduce total label column. Distinct category codes remain separate even labels coincide. Cross-tabulations association tests tab2() fre2() report cell counts rather five percentages listed . .chi2 = TRUE, Pearson's chi-square test uses displayed categories, including missing ones. Filter missing categories beforehand contribute test. Empty rows columns excluded calculation. Let O_ij observed cell count, E_ij expected count independence, r number nonempty rows, c number nonempty columns, N total count: Expected counts: E_ij = row_total_i * column_total_j / N. Pearson's chi-square: X^2 = sum((O_ij - E_ij)^2 / E_ij). Degrees freedom: df = (r - 1) * (c - 1). p-value: Upper-tail probability chi-square distribution df degrees freedom. Cramer's V: sqrt(X^2 / (N * min(r - 1, c - 1))). 2--2 tables, signed phi coefficient, Stata, sign O_11 * O_22 - O_12 * O_21. Frequency weights act cell counts test. Analytic weights supported; complex survey designs, use survey::svychisq(). Cross-tabulation category values become column names, conflicts reserved names "total" may require recoding. Computed variables groups Named expressions ... evaluated ungrouped data, counts calculated within groups. Use grouped dplyr::mutate() first group-specific computations. Input column names conflict output columns renamed result; input data unchanged.

code: var_type(1:10) #> [1] "integer"  var_type(1:10, abbr = TRUE) #> [1] "int"  var_type(letters) #> [1] "character"  # Compare storage, dispatch classes and readable type labels objects <- list(   score = 1.5,   grade = ordered(c("low", "high"), levels = c("low", "high")),   recorded = as.POSIXct("2026-01-01", tz = "UTC"),   answer = haven::labelled(c(1, 2), labels = c(Yes = 1, No = 2)) )  purrr::map(objects, \(x) tibble::tibble(   typeof = typeof(x),   class = paste(class(x), collapse = ", "),   var_type = var_type(x) )) |>   purrr::list_rbind(names_to = "variable") #> # A tibble: 4 × 4 #>   variable typeof  class                              var_type     #>   <chr>    <chr>   <chr>                              <chr>        #> 1 score    double  numeric                            double       #> 2 grade    integer ordered, factor                    ordered      #> 3 recorded double  POSIXct, POSIXt                    datetime     #> 4 answer   double  haven_labelled, vctrs_vctr, double double+label  # Type and unit describe different properties of the same object elapsed <- as.difftime(c(1, 2, 3), units = "hours") elapsed #> Time differences in hours #> [1] 1 2 3  var_type(elapsed) #> [1] "duration"  var_unit(elapsed) #> [1] "hours"
